before_times: The kind of event: a party, a wedding, a company or school event
The date, and the start and end time
The venue's name and town (for the travel fee), and indoors, outdoors or both
About how many guests (it sets the sound system)
Add-ons: uplighting, a second room, ceremony sound
At the studio: the lesson and the level, or the rental night
after_time: The music styles, and any kids at the event (clean edits)
A mic for toasts or announcements?
The venue contact and their mobile, if they'll be there
The venue's rules: load-in time and door, power, sound limit, music curfew, an insurance certificate
Must-play and do-not-play songs and the timeline (on the music form later)
secure_page_only: The venue's gate or door codes
Access needs, like a guest in a wheelchair near the speakers
Names and how to say them, for the MC
Family notes, like guests to keep apart in announcements
A child's name and age (kids' lessons and parties)
intake_questions.who_may_book: An adult. For a wedding, either partner may book, and both may sign. A parent books a kids' party or a child's lesson. A company party: someone the company names.

stop.words: Someone hurt, a fire, or a fight at the venue right now
stop.says: If anyone is hurt or in danger, call 911 now.
stop.booking: No booking until it's safe; the customer can come back.

go_on.words: A speaker or cable that's smoking, sparking or wet
go_on.says: Unplug it only if it's safe to reach, and keep everyone back. If there's fire, call 911.

safety_and_stop_words.always: Always on: danger to life, fire, gas, or a medical emergency gets 'call 911' first.

prep: The final timeline and the do-not-play list, 2 days before
The venue contact's mobile, and where the DJ loads in and parks
A table and an outlet near the dance floor, if the venue doesn't set them
At the studio: bring headphones if you have them, and arrive 10 minutes early

staff.supervision: None by state rule. A second DJ or a lighting tech works with a lead on the same event. A background check first where a school or the state form asks.
staff.who_oks: The owner OKs every wedding, every venue not on file, every quote over the limit and any stand-in lead. Overtime and extras need the customer's written yes, and the owner's OK only over the limit. An office manager may OK prices if the owner sets it.
staff.stand_in: A lead DJ the owner trusts, even from outside the team. The customer is asked first and may take a full refund instead. With no answer by the evening before, the stand-in plays as the contract allows, the owner calls, and a full refund stays open until the event starts. For a wedding, the owner calls the couple too. The music form and the timeline go with the gig.
roles: Second DJ (a second room, or kids' parties)

children_and_age.who_may_book: An adult. For a wedding, either partner may book, and both may sign. A parent books a kids' party or a child's lesson. A company party: someone the company names.
children_and_age.minors_texts: A parent books a kids' party or a child's lesson. Clips of a child are posted only with a parent's signed yes.

visit.done: The DJ texts DONE after load-out, with any overtime played.

license.note: Optional. Upload anything. Rosie never checks it and never shows it as checked (D96).
license.need: None for DJ work in most places. A local business license where the city or county asks for one: from the state form.
license.who: The business holds any business license. DJs and instructors need no license of their own.
ask: The business license number, where the city or county asks for one
The liability insurance policy and its end date
license.insurance: Liability insurance on file, with its end date. Many venues ask for a certificate naming them, sent before the event.
license.background: Only where the state form or the venue asks, like for a school dance.

never_in_a_text: Gate codes, access notes, a child's details and family notes stay on the secure page. The do-not-play list and the timeline stay on the music form. Texts to the DJ carry none of them either.
